title: Collections: registry, stream, list, log, ledger, cache, snapshot, tracker, inbox

answer.summary: The Web Tools estate calls its collections of records by nine overlapping words. Four AI agents mapped them separately and reached one answer. Two questions decide what to call a collection: does an entry stand for a thing or an event, and does it change after it is written? Four more words add to the name when they apply.

cells.note: session records, now called a stream
a reading kept as of its date

add.when: its entries are rebuilt from other files
each entry carries a status, such as open or done
someone chooses the members by hand

renames.from: snapshot, for a copy rebuilt in place (the constellation atlas, the occurrence index)
renames.why: It is rebuilt from other files, which is what cache means.

renames.becomes: the empty box's word, still open
renames.why: A session record is rewritten while the session runs, so it is not a stream.
It holds several collections and is not one.

open.question: Which one word covers events that never change: stream, log or ledger?
open.why: docs/registries.md already defines it; log and ledger can stay as informal names for it.

open.question: What word fits an event whose record changes while it is live, such as a session record?
Request files closed by adding a result file (errands, proposals) never change either, but are not snapshots. What should they be called?
open.why: Reader A's proposal: a standard term that collides with nothing in the estate's vocabulary. Reader D found the same gap.

open.question: Should a collection that drops its oldest entries past a cap get its own word, window?
open.why: Only Reader D raised it, for chron/sweeps.md and the calls record.

answer.by: Drawn from the four maps by the session that set the test; each row lists the readers whose maps state it.

steps.gloss: List each word and each distinct way the documents use it, with the line that uses it.
steps.example: "Snapshot" is used two ways: a dated reading kept as written, and a copy rebuilt in place.

steps.gloss: Turn what the senses imply into a few questions, each with a fixed set of answers.
steps.example: What does one entry stand for, a thing or an event? Does it change after it is written?

steps.gloss: Find the collections each word is used for, add some no word is used for, and answer every question for each.
steps.example: About thirty collections, such as task files, a news log and several caches.

steps.gloss: A script flags a question that tells nothing apart, two things no question tells apart, and a combination of answers nothing has. The reader answers each flag.
steps.example: Reader A could not tell two rebuilt copies apart, so added the question "Who rebuilds it?"

steps.gloss: Say what kind of category each sense turned out to be: one answer to one question, a box on two, or membership in a list.
steps.example: Stream, log and ledger are one box.

runs.method: cat-map skill, steps 1 to 4: senses and their requires read from the defining documents sentence by sentence; characteristics gathered from the senses and from comparing unsure pairs; instances found by searching the three checkouts and counted as referents; every instance coded on every characteristic; separation-checks.py run with --write and each finding answered; proposed names checked against web-tools' declared vocabulary with skills/concept-index/vocab.py (index written to stdout, not to disk). The first run left the unsure pair constellation-atlas and activity-cache unseparated; rebuilt_by was added in answer, from manifest.md:278-279 (a cold cache is rebuilt by its reader) against web-tools-private/README.md:80 and :84 (the atlas and entities.json are rebuilt elsewhere), with entities-json and source-bundle added as instances.

categories.sense: A collection whose entries stand for events at the time they happened and are never edited; a later entry corrects an earlier one. Declared in a manifest stores block.

categories.sense: A stream entry whose content is a registry as it stood at one time, such as a dated reading of the checks; not restamped.
categories.verdict: Holds for the checks reading, delivery.json and source bundles. Defined as a stream entry, but its rows stand for things and never change: it is the (thing, never changed) cell that registry and stream leave out, a third value on those two axes.

categories.sense: The latest derived copy of some state, replaced on each refresh (daily atlas, daily text occurrences, monthly bill data).
categories.verdict: Applied to derived files replaced daily or monthly (constellation atlas, text occurrences, wsl-sync data); nothing but the word separates them from entities.json, which is called a cache, and they share only the word with the dated sense. Call them caches rebuilt elsewhere and keep 'snapshot' for dated readings.

categories.sense: A derived copy kept so the app can read across repos without a live scan; never hand-edited, rewritten by a crawl only when its content changed.
categories.verdict: Holds for the state/ files: derived, replaced in place, may lag, never hand-edited. It fixes provenance and currency, not the registry and stream axes (cache rows stand for things in the activity cache and occurrences in the sessions cache); rebuilt_by splits the reader-rebuilt crawl caches from entities.json.

categories.sense: One of the lists the Lists view holds: To-do, Jot, Pin, Snag, created lists, and also Ping (errands) and Note (notes).
categories.verdict: Membership in the Lists view is the only thing it fixes: members take every value of stands_for and after_written (to-dos and snags are edited things, jots are material that leaves, Note is an appended stream, Ping is errands). Say 'a Lists view list' and name each member's shape with the other words.

categories.sense: Any enumeration of members: the estate membership list, the guided reading list.
categories.verdict: Plain English for any enumeration (a curated registry, a derived membership): no edge, no implication, not a collection kind.
categories.where: web-tools/docs/manifest.md:239-259; web-tools/docs/registries.csv:30 (aims-reading target 'a document on the guided reading list')

categories.sense: A dated, durable record of what happened, added to over time: the running log, the outer log, a task's progress log, the app's traffic log.
categories.verdict: Same cell as stream, met by the news ledger, progress logs and traffic logs; the running log, chron/, does not meet it, since its entries are dated documents and 69 of 315 were changed after creation. Keep log as an undeclared synonym of stream; call chron by its own name.

categories.sense: An append-only record that is never rewritten: the news ledger, the PowerShell outpost observations ledger, the page's call ledger.
categories.verdict: Same cell as stream and log, met by the news ledger and the outpost observations CSV; the page's call ledger also drops its oldest past 400. A third word for one cell.

categories.sense: An accounting-style table of financial actions: Budget DRS's decision (enacted) ledger, one row per budget item enacted in a session, and the state's general ledger.
categories.verdict: Rows are enacted budget items per session, derived and rebuilt by build-decision-ledger.py, so it shares only stands_for with the append-only ledger. A domain term from accounting, not a collection kind; in the collection vocabulary it is a derived table held by a check, the (occurrence, changed in place) cell.

categories.sense: A workspace's task files, one per task, edited as a task moves through backlog, in-progress, blocked and done, with generated rollups; committed to main in real time.
categories.verdict: Holds for tracker task files: the registry cell plus an open-then-closed lifecycle, with a stream inside (the progress log) and projections beside it (board.md, board.csv). A value on the lifecycle axis, not an alternative to registry; to-dos, errands and proposals carry the same lifecycle without the word.

categories.sense: A receiver's declared landing folder for a deposit that names no directory; drained, so it trends toward empty.
categories.verdict: Holds for chron/dump and fixes the leaves axis (removed once placed elsewhere), which no other word fixes. shortcuts/incoming and the Jot list behave the same way without the word, and web-tools-private declares inbox: inbox with no inbox/ folder.

outcome.summary: A mix. Registry, stream and snapshot are alternatives on one plane, what an entry stands for crossed with whether it is edited, and fill three of its four cells; log and ledger are near-synonyms of stream; tracker and inbox are regions that add a done state or a drain; cache is a value on the provenance axis that crosses every shape; the declared registry, the Lists view and the state/ caches are curated memberships; the registry repo and the environment snapshot are other kinds of thing. The fourth cell, occurrence records edited after writing (session records, chron entries), has no word of its own, and both are called stream.

outcome.summary: A mix, mostly values on different axes. Only stream, ledger and the dated log are rivals: they share one region (an event, never edited, kept) and differ by nothing in the files, while registry and snapshot each fix what an entry stands for and how it changes, cache fixes provenance and how it is kept current, inbox fixes only whether entries leave, tracker is the registry shape plus a growing dated part, and the CSV registry and the Lists view list are curated lists with no separating characteristic of their own. Three senses (the registry repository, the environment snapshot, the 'ledger, not a ban' count) are not collections at all. Usage drifts where a word is applied by its look: session records and jots called streams, the atlas and the ui-units file called snapshots though they are caches, the request ledger trimmed to 400 rows, an unlisted CSV called a registry. The gaps are real: user calls, snags and to-dos are trackers or registries in shape under no such word, web-tools' dump/ is a tray nothing drains, and no .web-tools.json in the three repositories carries the stores block that was to make registries and streams by declaration. What is there is a few shapes (an entry per thing edited in place, an entry per event kept as written, a dated reading kept as written, a current-state cache, an inbox) crossed with provenance and with whether each entry carries its own growing log.

characteristics.label: What does one entry stand for: a thing found by a key, an event at its time, a thing as it stood at one fixed time, or material set down to be routed elsewhere?
What happens to an entry once it is written: rewritten to track its subject, kept while new ones are added, dropped when a bound is passed, removed once handled, or never touched again?
How it came to be, which says what losing it costs: authored, derived (rebuilt if lost) or captured (gone if lost), in web-tools-private's three layers.
Does an entry carry a work state (open, done, closed, staged) that someone acts on?
How the entries are stored.
Which curated roster names the collection: web-tools docs/registries.csv, the Lists view, the State view, or none.
Which .web-tools.json key declares the collection: a stores entry, inbox, a single-path key (notes, sessions, captures), tracker, bundles, or none.

outcome.summary: A mix. Registry in its defining sense, stream, snapshot in its defined sense, log, ledger, tracker and inbox are values on one pair of axes, what an entry stands for and what happens to it once written; on that pair stream, log and ledger are near-synonyms (event, appended), and tracker nests inside registry (a registry with a status and one file per entry). Cache, and snapshot as it is actually used, sit on a different axis, provenance: either names any derived copy, so one environment image is called both. List and the governed registry are rosters, membership in the Lists view or in registries.csv, on no shape axis at all, and registry also names a repository. The declared-stream standard admits nothing, because no repository declares a stores block. Misfits: the installed-app registry (a dated capture), prune.json as a ledger (edited per shortcut), calls.json as a cache (a captured run record), session records as a stream (rewritten while live), occurrences.json as a snapshot (overwritten daily). Gaps no word covers: a rolling window (sweeps.md, calls.json, the runs rings), a thing kept as an append-only stream (tending findings, errands and proposals closed by a result file that web-tools-private/proposals/README.md calls a tombstone), run state such as cursors, and a tray nobody drains. What is there is better named by two declared fields than by a noun: grain (thing, event, as-of, deposit) and change (updated, appended, rolling, drained, frozen), with provenance beside them; the nouns can then be reserved: registry for thing and updated, stream for event and appended, snapshot for as-of and frozen, window for event and rolling, inbox for deposit and drained, and cache for any derived copy.

agreement.finding: Registry, stream and snapshot sit on one plane: what an entry stands for, crossed with whether it changes after it is written.
Stream, log and ledger name the same cell; nothing in the files separates them.
Cache is a value of where entries come from (provenance), crossing every shape.
Tracker is the registry shape plus a status or a growing dated part.
Inbox fixes only whether entries leave.
The Lists view's list is curated membership, on no shape axis.
Registry in the registries.csv sense is curated membership, on no shape axis.
"Registry" for web-tools-private names a repository, not a collection.
Session records are called a stream but are rewritten while the session runs.
"Snapshot" names both a dated reading kept as written and a derived copy replaced in place.
No repository declares the stores block that registries.md says declares a stream.
web-tools/dump/ is a tray nothing drains.
A rolling window (chron/sweeps.md, state/calls.json) has no word.
